deep.reconstruction:
Context: notes for Grothendieck's Nov.–Dec. 1967 IHES lectures on crystals, which became 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968). The previous page introduced Washnitzer–Monsky (W.M.) cohomology: the hypercohomology of the de Rham complexes Ω•_{A/W} of (weakly complete) lifts A of special affine opens, on a site of such lifts with a Zariski-type topology. The page then began a 'Critique de W.M.' and listed its merits. This page continues the merits.

(1) The coefficient ring is W(k), the Witt vectors. Its fraction field K has characteristic 0, not characteristic p as k does. So the theory yields a Weil-type cohomology with coefficients in characteristic 0. This answers a main criticism of naive de Rham cohomology in characteristic p, whose coefficients lie in k.

(2) Because the theory is integral (it lives over W(k), not just over K), it gives a notion of p-adic torsion. Grothendieck suggests this may be 'the right one'. He asks whether, for a lift X/W, the torsion of this integral cohomology agrees with the p-adic torsion of the étale cohomology of the geometric generic fibre X_{\bar K}.

(3) He places this inside what he calls the extremely important and deep question: how de Rham cohomology relates to p-adic (étale) cohomology under specialization from characteristic 0 to characteristic p > 0. He notes Tate already studied this 'in a different language' for H^1 of abelian varieties, via p-divisible groups and Hodge–Tate decompositions; this is presumably Tate's 1966 Driebergen talk. He stresses its importance for certain facts about families of algebraic cycles, referring to his own text in Inventiones, possibly 'Un théorème sur les homomorphismes de schémas abéliens', Invent. Math. 2 (1966). That reference is uncertain given the words 'à paraître prochainement'.

The page is programmatic: it motivates an integral p-adic cohomology (later crystalline cohomology) and announces what later became the 'mysterious functor' problem and p-adic Hodge theory.
errors: The reading 'car. k' in line 3 is probably 'et non k', i.e. characteristic 0 rather than that of k; it is not a mathematical error.

The implied hope that integral W.M. cohomology gives good torsion was too optimistic. Integral Monsky–Washnitzer cohomology is not finitely generated over W, as Grothendieck himself complains on the next page; only its K-tensored version (and later crystalline cohomology) behaves well.

Equality of crystalline torsion with étale torsion of the geometric generic fibre is false in general. Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze (2018) prove only an inequality (étale torsion length ≤ crystalline torsion length, for smooth proper X over O_C) and give examples where it is strict. Grothendieck poses it only as a question, so this is not an error on his part.

ideas.what: Integral p-adic cohomology with coefficients in W(k), whose fraction field has characteristic 0, as an answer to the defect of naive char-p de Rham cohomology
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes (Dix exposés, 1968), introduction

ideas.what: Question whether the torsion of integral p-adic (crystalline-type) cohomology of the special fibre equals the p-torsion of étale cohomology of the geometric generic fibre
ideas.modern_name: Comparison of torsion in crystalline vs p-adic étale cohomology (integral p-adic Hodge theory; A_inf-cohomology)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Fontaine–Messing, Faltings, Caruso (small-ramification cases); Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze 2018 (general inequality and counterexamples to equality)
ideas.where_published: Possibly hinted at in Crystals (1968) and in the 1970 ICM talk 'Groupes de Barsotti–Tate et cristaux'; the explicit torsion question is unsure

ideas.what: Relation between de Rham cohomology in characteristic 0 and p-adic étale cohomology under specialization to characteristic p, following Tate for H^1 of abelian varieties
ideas.modern_name: p-adic Hodge theory / Grothendieck's 'mysterious functor' / p-adic comparison theorems
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tate (1967), Grothendieck (1970), Fontaine (1979–82), Faltings, Fontaine–Messing, Tsuji
ideas.where_published: ICM 1970 'Groupes de Barsotti–Tate et cristaux'; Crystals (1968)

ideas.what: Link between this p-adic comparison problem and families of algebraic cycles
ideas.modern_name: (p-adic) variational Hodge conjecture / deformation of cycle classes
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (variational Hodge, 1966); Fontaine–Messing, Emerton; Bloch–Esnault–Kerz (2014) for the p-adic version
ideas.where_published: Variational Hodge appears in 'On the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties' (1966, footnote); the Inventiones reference here is uncertain

missed.claim: Already in 1966–67 Grothendieck explicitly asked whether integral p-adic (W-)cohomology of the special fibre has the same torsion as p-adic étale cohomology of the geometric generic fibre. This is the question resolved, negatively in general and as an inequality, by Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze. It is an early, explicit formulation not usually attributed to him.
missed.quote: fournit une notion de torsion p-adique, qui est peut-être la bonne : est-ce la torsion p-adique de la fibre générique géométrique ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical attribution of the integral torsion-comparison question in p-adic Hodge theory, central to A_inf/prismatic work, to Grothendieck about 50 years before its resolution.

missed.claim: He ties the de Rham ↔ p-adic specialization problem to the study of families of algebraic cycles. This anticipates the p-adic variational Hodge conjecture (Fontaine–Messing, Emerton, Bloch–Esnault–Kerz), which is not usually traced back to Grothendieck's crystal notes.
missed.quote: sur l'importance de cette question pour l'étude de certains faits liés aux familles de cycles algébriques
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical precursor for the p-adic variational Hodge conjecture and deformation of cycles from characteristic p to mixed characteristic.

deep.surprise_reason: Most of the page restates motivation that appears in the published Crystals text and the 1970 ICM talk. The explicit question about torsion of integral cohomology versus étale torsion of the geometric generic fibre, and the explicit link to families of cycles, are noteworthy early formulations. They are not results, however, and the general theme is known to be Grothendieck's.
transcription_corrections: Line 3: 'et car. k' is likely 'et non k' (characteristic 0, not that of k).
'(c'est-à-dire vraie qu'elle soit dans W(k), pas sur K)' likely reads '(c'est-à-dire le fait qu'elle soit dans W(k), pas sur K)'.
'Tous [?] est vraisemblablement la question' is likely 'Ici est soulevée la question' or similar.
'dans son [?] séminaire [?] de l'an dernier' may refer to Tate's Driebergen 1966 lecture on p-divisible groups; the reading is uncertain.
'cf mes leçons aux Inventiones [ ] / à paraître prochainement': the venue word is uncertain; it may refer to Grothendieck's Inventiones 1966 paper or to a forthcoming text.
